newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester announces sale auction.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester announces sale auction.

text.p: Britain's Alliance & Leicester Building Society said on Thursday it would auction those free shares which members decided they wanted to sell via a free dealing service when the group is floated later this month.

"The sale shares of those recipients of the free shares who have elected to use the free dealing service will be sold by means of a series of auctions starting on Friday April 18, 1997," the group said in a statement, adding that the number of sale shares and auctions would be announced next week.

Alliance & Leicester, one of Britain's traditional home loan providers, is due to be listed on the London Stock Exchange on April 21, said those who wished to bid in the auctions had to complete a pre-registration form and return it to stockbrokers Cazenove & Co by 1600 GMT on April 16.

It said the sale shares would be aggregated and sold by Cazenove as agent for the sellers "by means of a series of two or three auctions and, if applicable, by market sales". The number of auctions depends on the number of sales and will be decided by Cazenove in consultation with the London Stock Exchange. The first will be on April 18.
The building society, which is ditching its mutual status in favour of becoming a listed company with effectively bank status, said shares would be sold to the highest bidder or bidders.

All eligible investing and borrowing members of the converting society will each receive 250 free shares in the new Alliance & Leicester Plc. It has said it will issue a total of 582 million shares an the flotation is expected to value it at around 2.5 billion pounds ($4.1 billion), with the exact value set by the market on the day of flotation. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
